questions.q: What makes something a fixed asset?
options: The company buys it to use, not to sell, and uses it for more than a year
It costs more than DKK 1,000
It is bought from a foreign supplier
It is sold to customers within a month
questions.reason: Fixed assets such as machines, vehicles, buildings and IT are used in the business for more than one year. Oak timber is not: it goes into tables and is sold.

questions.q: Why is the CNC machine not booked as a DKK 600,000 expense in January?
options: Its cost is spread over its useful life through depreciation, because it helps the business for ten years
Expenses can only be posted in December
Because the VAT has not been paid yet
Because machines never affect the P&L
questions.reason: Depreciation spreads the cost over the years the machine is used, so January does not look terrible and the next years too good.

questions.q: With straight-line depreciation over 10 years, how much is the CNC machine depreciated each month?
questions.reason: DKK 600,000 ÷ 10 years = DKK 60,000 a year, and 60,000 ÷ 12 = DKK 5,000 a month.

questions.q: What is the CNC machine's book value after the March 2026 depreciation run?
questions.reason: Three months of DKK 5,000 is 15,000 accumulated depreciation, and 600,000 − 15,000 = 585,000.

questions.q: Which transaction creates an asset master record?
options: AS01
AFAB
OB52
FAGLGVTR
questions.reason: AS01 creates the asset master record, the asset's ID card. AFAB posts depreciation, OB52 opens and closes periods and FAGLGVTR carries balances forward.

questions.q: What does the asset class decide?
options: The GL accounts the asset posts to and its default depreciation rules
The supplier the asset is bought from
The VAT rate on the invoice
The posting period that is open
questions.reason: The asset class (here Machinery and equipment) groups assets and points them to accounts such as 211000, 211900 and 481000, with default depreciation settings.

questions.q: Why does SAP keep more than one depreciation area for the same asset?
options: Tax rules differ from book rules, so each purpose gets its own values and method
To store the asset in two company codes
To post depreciation twice to the P&L
Because each cost centre needs its own area
questions.reason: Book depreciation (area 01) is for the financial statements; Danish tax rules differ, so a separate tax area holds the tax values.

questions.q: How do the asset sub-ledger and GL account 211000 relate?
options: 211000 is the reconciliation account: it holds the total of all machinery assets, posted through the assets
211000 is updated once a year from the sub-ledger
Users post directly to 211000 and assets are optional
211000 holds only depreciation
questions.reason: Like supplier and customer reconciliation accounts, 211000 shows the total while the sub-ledger keeps each asset. Every posting goes through an asset, so they always agree.

questions.q: When Nordlys buys the machine, what is the integrated acquisition posting?
options: Debit 211000 600,000, debit 154000 Input VAT 150,000, credit 160000 Payables 750,000
Debit 211000 750,000, credit 160000 Payables 750,000
questions.reason: The net cost goes onto the asset, the 25% VAT is input VAT Nordlys gets back from SKAT, and the supplier is owed the gross DKK 750,000.

questions.q: Why is the DKK 150,000 VAT not part of the machine's cost?
options: It is input VAT that Nordlys gets back from SKAT through the VAT return
VAT is always depreciated separately over 5 years
VAT is paid by the supplier
VAT belongs to cost centre 1000
questions.reason: Input VAT is recoverable, so it sits on 154000 and is offset in the VAT return, not added to the asset.

questions.q: What does the Asset Explorer (AW01N) show?
options: An asset's values per year and area, including planned and posted depreciation
Open supplier invoices
Bank statement lines
The posting period settings
questions.reason: AW01N shows acquisition value, planned and posted depreciation and book value for each depreciation area and fiscal year.

questions.q: What does the monthly depreciation run (AFAB) post for the CNC machine?
options: Debit 481000 Depreciation (cost centre 1000) 5,000, credit 211900 Accumulated depreciation 5,000
questions.reason: The expense goes to 481000 on cost centre 1000 and the depreciation piles up on 211900. The original cost on 211000 is not touched.

questions.q: Nordlys sells the CNC machine on 31.12.2028 for DKK 450,000 net, when its book value is 420,000. What is the result?
options: A gain of DKK 30,000
A loss of DKK 30,000
A gain of DKK 450,000
No gain or loss
questions.reason: Sale price 450,000 minus book value 420,000 (600,000 − 36 × 5,000) = a gain of 30,000.

questions.q: What is true about an asset under construction (AuC)?
options: It collects costs while something is being built, is not depreciated, and is settled to a normal asset when ready
It is depreciated faster than normal assets
It is an expense posted straight to the P&L
It can only be used for buildings bought ready-made
questions.reason: An AuC is not in use yet, so it is not depreciated. When ready it is settled to a final asset and depreciation starts.

questions.q: Why does Peter post an accrual of DKK 12,000 for the external accountant's March bookkeeping support on 31.03?
options: The work was done in March but the invoice comes in April, so the cost must be shown in March
Because the accountant was paid twice
To move costs from March into April
Because accounting fees are a fixed asset
questions.reason: An accrual puts a cost into the period it belongs to before the invoice arrives: debit 476500 Accounting and audit fees (cost centre 3000), credit 190000 Accrued expenses.

questions.q: Why does the March electricity (DKK 18,000) need no accrual at month-end?
options: It was already billed and paid on 04.03, so it is already in March
Electricity is never a cost
It is depreciated instead
It is posted in period 13
questions.reason: Only costs that belong to March but have no invoice yet are accrued. Electricity was posted and paid on 04.03, so accruing it would charge March twice.

questions.q: What happens to the accounting fees accrual on 01.04.2026?
options: It is reversed, so when the real invoice is posted in April the two cancel out
It is paid to the supplier automatically
It is depreciated over 12 months
It stays on 190000 for the rest of the year
questions.reason: The accrual has a reversal date of 01.04. The reversal and the April invoice cancel out, so the cost appears only once, in March.

questions.q: A EUR 10,000 supplier invoice was booked at 7.46. At month-end the rate is 7.45. What does FAGL_FCV post?
options: An unrealised gain of DKK 100, because Nordlys now owes less in DKK
An unrealised loss of DKK 100
A realised gain of DKK 1,000
Nothing, because the invoice is not paid
questions.reason: 10,000 × 7.46 = 74,600 and 10,000 × 7.45 = 74,500. The payable drops by DKK 100: an unrealised gain, because it isn't paid yet.

questions.q: Why are CO allocations (step 7) run after accruals and depreciation?
options: So that all March costs are on the cost centres before they are shared out
Because allocations close the posting period
Because allocations create the VAT report
Because they must run before any invoice is posted
questions.reason: Allocations share out what is on the cost centres. Running them earlier would miss the accrual and depreciation costs.

questions.q: In the story, how much VAT does Nordlys pay SKAT for March 2026?
questions.reason: Output VAT 30,000 on the sale minus input VAT 20,000 on the oak = DKK 10,000 to pay in the momsangivelse.

questions.q: What does Peter do in OB52 at the end of the close?
options: Closes posting period 03.2026 and opens 04.2026 so nobody posts into March by accident
Runs the depreciation
Revalues foreign currency
Creates the asset master record
questions.reason: OB52 controls which posting periods are open. Closing March protects the numbers that have been reported.

questions.q: Which statement about the balance sheet and P&L is correct?
options: The P&L shows a period's revenue minus costs; the balance sheet shows assets = liabilities + equity on one day
Both show only cash in the bank
The balance sheet shows revenue and the P&L shows assets
They are not linked in any way
questions.reason: The P&L is a video of a period, the balance sheet a photo of one day. The profit for the period becomes part of equity.

questions.q: In the tiny March example, assets are DKK 982,000 and liabilities are DKK 196,500. What must equity be?
questions.reason: Assets = liabilities + equity, so equity = 982,000 − 196,500 = 785,500 (750,400 earlier equity plus 35,100 March profit).

questions.q: What are special periods 13 to 16 used for?
options: Year-end adjustments, such as auditor corrections, that belong to the old year but are kept apart from December
Extra months for the next year
Posting depreciation for assets under construction
Storing tax depreciation
questions.reason: Special periods belong to the same fiscal year and use the posting date 31.12, so December's own figures stay clean.

questions.q: What does the balance carry-forward (FAGLGVTR) do?
options: Moves balance sheet balances into the new year and puts the year's profit or loss into retained earnings
Closes the asset fiscal year
Posts the monthly depreciation
Revalues foreign currency items
questions.reason: Balance sheet accounts carry their balances into 2027, while P&L accounts start at zero and the result goes to equity.

questions.q: What does asset year-end closing (AJAB) do?
options: Locks the asset fiscal year so no more asset postings go into it
Opens period 13
Carries GL balances forward
Creates the annual report for Erhvervsstyrelsen
questions.reason: AJAB closes the fiscal year in asset accounting. It only works when all depreciation for the year has been posted without errors.

questions.q: Sofie finds an open item on 191100 GR/IR clearing during the close. What does it usually mean?
options: Goods were received but not invoiced yet, or invoiced but not received yet
The bank statement is missing
The asset has been sold
VAT was posted twice
questions.reason: GR/IR clears when both the goods receipt and the invoice are posted. Leftovers need an owner and an explanation during the close.
